question.text: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA) read with DPDP Rules 2025, when an AIF collects personal data from an investor for onboarding, the consent obtained from the investor must be:

answer.text: Free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, with clear and plain language NOTICE describing the personal data, purpose of processing, rights of data principal, and grievance mechanism
Implicit based on signing the subscription form
Given only once at fund inception; no re-consent required for subsequent processing

explanation.text: The Logic: Under DPDPA 2023, consent must be FREE, SPECIFIC, INFORMED, UNCONDITIONAL and UNAMBIGUOUS, expressed through clear affirmative action. The data fiduciary (AIF) must provide a NOTICE describing: the personal data proposed to be collected, purpose of processing, how data principals may exercise rights (access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal), and the manner to withdraw consent. Data principal has the right to withdraw consent at any time with prospective effect. The Trap: Option B (implicit) violates the 'affirmative action' standard. Option C fails to address dynamic re-consent needs. Option D discriminates by nationality (not permitted). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers DPDPA. GDPR (EU) has similar framework — useful cross-reference for foreign LPs. CSCRF 2024 + DPDPA 2023 form the twin data-governance pillars for SEBI REs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Structure your Subscription Agreement so consent checkboxes are unbundled (one box per purpose: KYC, marketing, FATCA reporting, ancillary services). Bundled consent can be invalidated by DPDPA Board. Train front-office to walk LPs through the privacy notice at onboarding — don't bury it in fine print.
